title: Player Tracking Data in Sports
abstract: There has been rapid growth in the collection of player tracking data in recent years. These data, providing spatiotemporal locations of players and ball at high resolution, have spurred methodological developments in a range of sports. There have been impacts in the development of player performance measurement (e.g., distance traveled) and in the attribution of value to specific plays (e.g., expected points from a given position) or even specific actions within a play. This review highlights key methodological contributions via statistical and machine learning approaches. The studies and outcomes discussed show how sports can be a playground for extending analytical techniques in a range of areas. The review also describes the ongoing methodological challenges associated with the use of tracking data.

title: Research on Volleyball Player Motion Trajectory Tracking Based on Gaussian Mixture Filtering Algorithm
abstract: In the field of computer technology based vision and motion tracking, traditional motion trajectory tracking methods often rely on basic linear filtering algorithms, which struggle to accurately predict and track an athlete’s trajectory in complex environments. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a novel trajectory tracking method for volleyball players based on the Gaussian Mixture Filter (GMF) algorithm. This method models the athlete’s movement on the volleyball court and leverages the probability distribution characteristics of the Gaussian Mixture Model to significantly improve trajectory estimation accuracy, particularly in complex settings. First, the athlete’s position data from consecutive image frames is processed using Gaussian Mixture Filtering to extract dynamic features. Then, a state-space model is built based on the athlete’s historical trajectory data, and the Kalman filter is applied to optimize the trajectory prediction. By analyzing the image frame sequence, the athlete’s position and speed at different time points are obtained, and the Gaussian Mixture Filter algorithm is used to accurately predict the motion trajectory. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and real-time performance in volleyball player trajectory tracking, showing substantial improvements over traditional methods, especially in high-speed movements or sudden direction changes, where it effectively reduces tracking errors. As a result, this method offers robust technical support for precise trajectory tracking and tactical analysis in volleyball.
venue: Advances in Transdisciplinary Engineering IOS Press
